# TypeScript Web Stack and Browser Interaction Plan

## Context

eCom Gliders migration requirements (from completed research):
- **328 blog posts** at root-level URLs (must preserve exactly)
- **26 pages** + service pages, case studies, free audit
- **Design target:** Tier B boutique premium (Olifant) + Tier C conversion (AMZ Dudes)
- **Key UX ask:** Cursor.com-style in-page browser mockups with tabbed views and smooth transitions
- **Content strategy (user decision):** JSON-configurable content in-repo now; CMS/admin panel integration later via abstraction layer

---

## Recommended stack (decision)

| Layer | Choice | Why |
|-------|--------|-----|
| Framework | **Next.js 15** (App Router) | SSR/SSG/ISR for SEO, metadata API, image optimization, catch-all routes for 328 blog URLs |
| Language | **TypeScript 5** (strict) | Type-safe content config, component props, schema validation |
| Styling | **Tailwind CSS v4** | `@theme` tokens in CSS, matches shadcn ecosystem, fast iteration |
| UI primitives | **shadcn/ui** (free, owned code) | Accessible Radix primitives, no vendor lock-in, CLI install |
| Animations | **Motion** (`motion/react`) | Tab transitions, browser content swaps, scroll reveals. NOT legacy `framer-motion` |
| Icons | **Lucide React** | shadcn default, professional, no Unicode symbols |
| Content (now) | **JSON + MDX files** | Configurable, version-controlled, CMS-ready abstraction |
| Content (future) | **Keystatic or Payload** via adapter | Plugs into same `ContentRepository` interface |
| Forms | **React Hook Form + Zod + Server Actions** | Type-safe validation, no client-side secrets |
| SEO | **next/metadata + schema-dts** | Per-page metadata, FAQPage/Organization/Service schema |
| Deployment | **Vercel** (proposed) | Native Next.js, ISR, edge, preview deploys |

**Not recommended:**
- Framer.com design exports as production code (not maintainable, poor SEO control)
- Pre-built paid block libraries (Tailark Pro, Aceternity Pro) -- build custom in-house instead
- Astro (weaker for interactive browser components + future CMS admin in same app)
- Plain React SPA (SEO penalty for 328 indexed posts)

---

## Architecture: CMS-ready content layer

User requirement: JSON-configurable now, CMS later. Use **Repository + Adapter pattern** so content source is swappable without touching UI components.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph ui [UI Layer]
        Pages[Page Components]
        Sections[Section Components]
        BrowserMock[BrowserMockup Component]
    end

    subgraph domain [Domain Layer]
        ContentRepo[ContentRepository Interface]
        PageService[PageService]
        BlogService[BlogService]
        NavService[NavigationService]
    end

    subgraph adapters [Content Adapters]
        JsonAdapter[JsonFileAdapter]
        MdxAdapter[MdxFileAdapter]
        FutureCms[FutureCmsAdapter]
    end

    subgraph data [Data Sources]
        JsonConfig["content/config/*.json"]
        MdxPosts["content/blog/*.mdx"]
        BackupMeta["backup/metadata/"]
    end

    Pages --> PageService
    Sections --> PageService
    BrowserMock --> PageService
    PageService --> ContentRepo
    BlogService --> ContentRepo
    NavService --> ContentRepo
    ContentRepo --> JsonAdapter
    ContentRepo --> MdxAdapter
    ContentRepo -.-> FutureCms
    JsonAdapter --> JsonConfig
    MdxAdapter --> MdxPosts
    MdxAdapter --> BackupMeta
```

### JSON config files (initial content source)

| File | Configures |
|------|-----------|
| `content/config/site.json` | Name, tagline, phone, email, address, social links, partner badges |
| `content/config/navigation.json` | Header nav, mega menu columns, footer columns, CTA labels |
| `content/config/homepage.json` | All 12 homepage sections (hero, stats, services, cases, FAQ, etc.) |
| `content/config/services/*.json` | Per-service page content (hero, stats, deliverables, FAQ) |
| `content/config/case-studies.json` | Case study index + card data |
| `content/config/testimonials.json` | Named quotes with role and company |
| `content/config/faq.json` | Shared and page-specific FAQ items |

### Blog content (MDX, separate from JSON)

328 posts migrate to `content/blog/{slug}.mdx` with frontmatter:
```typescript
interface BlogPostFrontmatter {
  title: string;
  slug: string;          // must match current URL exactly
  publishedAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  author: string;
  categories: string[];
  tags: string[];
  metaTitle: string;
  metaDescription: string;
  canonical: string;
  featuredImage: string;
  excerpt: string;
}
```

Routing: `app/[slug]/page.tsx` catch-all with static generation from slug inventory in [`backup/metadata/blog-inventory.json`](backup/metadata/blog-inventory.json).

### Domain interfaces (OOP, SOLID)

```typescript
// src/domain/content/content-repository.ts
interface ContentRepository {
  getSiteConfig(): Promise<SiteConfig>;
  getNavigation(): Promise<NavigationConfig>;
  getHomepage(): Promise<HomepageConfig>;
  getService(slug: string): Promise<ServicePageConfig | null>;
  getCaseStudies(): Promise<CaseStudyConfig[]>;
  getBlogPost(slug: string): Promise<BlogPost | null>;
  getAllBlogSlugs(): Promise<string[]>;
}

// src/infrastructure/content/json-content-repository.ts
class JsonContentRepository implements ContentRepository { ... }

// Future: src/infrastructure/content/payload-content-repository.ts
class PayloadContentRepository implements ContentRepository { ... }
```

UI components depend on `ContentRepository` interface, never on JSON files directly. Future CMS = swap adapter, zero page rewrites.

---

## Package stack (detailed)

### Core (install at scaffold)

| Package | Version | Purpose |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `next` | 15.x | Framework |
| `react` / `react-dom` | 19.x | UI |
| `typescript` | 5.x | Types |
| `tailwindcss` | 4.x | Styling via `@import "tailwindcss"` |
| `@tailwindcss/postcss` | 4.x | PostCSS plugin |
| `clsx` + `tailwind-merge` | latest | `cn()` helper |
| `class-variance-authority` | latest | Button/card variants |
| `zod` | latest | Config + form validation |

### shadcn/ui components to install (selective, not all 40+)

**Navigation and layout:**
- `navigation-menu` -- mega menu
- `sheet` -- mobile nav drawer
- `button`, `badge` -- CTAs and tags

**Content sections:**
- `accordion` -- FAQ (with FAQPage schema)
- `card` -- stat cards, service cards, case study cards
- `tabs` -- browser mockup tab switching, seller segmentation
- `separator` -- section dividers

**Forms:**
- `input`, `textarea`, `select`, `label`, `form` -- contact and audit forms
- `dialog` -- optional supplementary lead modal (not primary contact)

**Feedback:**
- `sonner` -- toast notifications on form submit

### Animation (free, MIT)

| Package | Purpose | Usage on eCom Gliders |
|---------|---------|----------------------|
| `motion` | Tab transitions, fade/blur content swaps, scroll reveals | Browser mockup, hero, case study cards |
| `@formkit/auto-animate` | List reorder animations | Optional for FAQ expand |

Import path: `import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react"` (always `"use client"` in App Router).

### SEO and metadata

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `schema-dts` | Type-safe JSON-LD (Organization, Service, FAQPage, BlogPosting) |
| `next-sitemap` | Auto sitemap from routes + blog slugs |

### Content processing

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `gray-matter` | Parse MDX frontmatter |
| `@next/mdx` or `next-mdx-remote` | Render blog MDX |
| `remark-gfm` | GitHub-flavored markdown (tables in blog posts) |
| `rehype-slug` + `rehype-autolink-headings` | TOC anchor links (preserve ez-toc behavior) |
| `reading-time` | Blog reading time meta |

### Forms and email

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `react-hook-form` | Form state |
| `@hookform/resolvers` | Zod integration |
| `resend` or `@react-email/components` | Transactional email for audit/contact forms |

### Dev tooling

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `eslint` + `eslint-config-next` | Linting |
| `prettier` + `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` | Formatting |
| `@playwright/test` | E2E (URL preservation verification) |
| `vitest` | Unit tests for content repository and validators |

---

## Free libraries to use (not build from scratch)

These are MIT/free, install via shadcn CLI, you own the code:

| Library | What to take | What NOT to take |
|---------|-------------|-----------------|
| **shadcn/ui** | All primitives listed above | Do not install entire catalog |
| **Magic UI** (free tier) | `marquee` (trust bar logos), `number-ticker` (stats), `animated-beam` (optional accent) | Skip particle effects, terminal animations (too SaaS-dev-tool) |
| **shadcn.io blocks** (free) | Reference layout for split hero, comparison table | Copy structure, rebuild with brand tokens |
| **Aceternity UI** (free components only) | Study `Hero Section With Tabs` browser pattern as reference | Do not use paid Pro blocks; build custom |

**Build in-house (user preference for paid-quality features):**
- Browser mockup chrome (tabs, URL bar, traffic lights)
- Tab-switching content panels with Motion transitions
- Mega menu with CTA panel
- Service page template
- Case study filter grid

---

## Custom Browser Mockup component (Cursor-style)

This is the centerpiece UX feature. Build as a reusable `BrowserMockup` component, not a third-party dependency.

### Reference patterns studied

| Source | Pattern | eCom Gliders adaptation |
|--------|---------|------------------------|
| cursor.com marketing | Split hero + product preview in browser frame | Amazon Seller Central / PPC dashboard views |
| Aceternity Hero With Tabs | Auto-rotating tabs, fade+blur transitions | Manual + auto tab switch for services |
| shadcn.io blocks | Tab-switch browser hero with AnimatePresence | Same technique, custom chrome |
| react-chrome-mockup | Pixel-accurate Chrome UI | Too heavy; build simplified chrome in-house |

### Component spec: `BrowserMockup`

```
src/components/browser-mockup/
  browser-mockup.tsx          # Main container (client component)
  browser-chrome.tsx          # Traffic lights + tab bar + URL bar
  browser-tab.tsx             # Individual tab
  browser-content-panel.tsx   # Animated content area
  browser-mockup.types.ts     # TabConfig, BrowserMockupProps
  index.ts
```

**Props interface:**
```typescript
interface BrowserTab {
  id: string;
  label: string;           // "PPC Dashboard", "Listing SEO", "Account Health"
  url: string;             // "sellercentral.amazon.com/ppc"
  content: React.ReactNode; // Screenshot, chart, or composed UI
}

interface BrowserMockupProps {
  tabs: BrowserTab[];
  defaultTab?: string;
  autoRotate?: boolean;     // Auto-switch every 8-10s
  autoRotateInterval?: number;
  className?: string;
}
```

**Animation behavior (Motion):**
- Tab click: `AnimatePresence` with `opacity: 0->1`, `y: 8->0`, `filter: blur(4px)->blur(0)` (200ms)
- Auto-rotate: pauses on hover, resumes on mouse leave
- URL bar: animates URL text on tab switch
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`: instant swap, no blur

**Accessibility:**
- Tabs are real `<button>` elements with `role="tablist"` / `role="tab"` / `role="tabpanel"`
- Keyboard: Arrow keys switch tabs
- `aria-selected` on active tab
- Content panels are not iframes (no accessibility trap)

### Where to use BrowserMockup on eCom Gliders

| Page | Section | Tab content |
|------|---------|-------------|
| Homepage hero | Right visual (replace static image) | Tab 1: PPC performance chart, Tab 2: Listing optimization score, Tab 3: Account health dashboard |
| Service: PPC | Hero or results section | Before/after ACOS, campaign structure, keyword report |
| Service: Listing SEO | Hero | Keyword ranking, listing score, search visibility |
| Case study detail | Results section | Client metrics dashboard mockup |
| Free audit page | "What you get" section | Sample audit report preview |
| Process section | Step visualization | Audit -> Strategy -> Execute -> Report as tab progression |

Content for each tab panel comes from JSON config (`homepage.json` -> `hero.browserTabs[]`), not hardcoded in component.

---

## Homepage section to package mapping

From [`.cursor/plans/2026-09-02-homepage-redesign-brief.md`](.cursor/plans/2026-09-02-homepage-redesign-brief.md):

| # | Section | Component source | Package |
|---|---------|-----------------|---------|
| 1 | Hero | Custom split layout + `BrowserMockup` | shadcn Button + Motion |
| 2 | Trust bar | Custom + Magic UI `marquee` | Magic UI (free) |
| 3 | Stats row | Custom `StatCard` x4 | shadcn Card + Magic UI `number-ticker` |
| 4 | Services | Custom `ServiceCard` 3x2 grid | shadcn Card |
| 5 | Who we serve | Custom tabs | shadcn Tabs |
| 6 | Case studies | Custom `CaseStudyCard` | shadcn Card + Motion hover |
| 7 | Process | Custom numbered steps | Lucide icons |
| 8 | Agency vs DIY | Custom comparison table | shadcn Table (build or native HTML) |
| 9 | Testimonials | Custom quote cards | shadcn Card |
| 10 | Blog insights | Custom post cards | next/image |
| 11 | FAQ | shadcn Accordion + FAQPage schema | shadcn Accordion |
| 12 | Final CTA | Custom CTA band + form link | shadcn Button |

---

## Project folder structure

```
ecomGliders/
  app/
    layout.tsx                    # Root layout, fonts, metadata
    page.tsx                      # Homepage (reads homepage.json)
    [slug]/page.tsx               # Blog posts (328 URLs)
    about-us/page.tsx
    contact/page.tsx
    case-studies/page.tsx
    case-studies/[slug]/page.tsx
    free-audit-2/page.tsx
    amazon-ppc-management-agency/page.tsx
    full-service-amazon-agency/page.tsx
    api/
      contact/route.ts            # Form handler
      audit/route.ts              # Audit form handler
  src/
    components/
      browser-mockup/             # Custom in-house (Cursor-style)
      layout/                     # Header, Footer, MegaMenu, MobileNav
      sections/                   # Hero, StatsRow, Services, FAQ, etc.
      ui/                         # shadcn primitives
    domain/
      content/                    # Interfaces, types, Zod schemas
      services/                   # PageService, BlogService
    infrastructure/
      content/                    # JsonContentRepository, MdxBlogRepository
    lib/
      utils.ts                    # cn()
      seo.ts                      # generateMetadata helpers
      schema.ts                   # JSON-LD builders
  content/
    config/                       # JSON files (homepage, nav, services, etc.)
    blog/                         # 328 MDX files (migrated)
  public/
    images/                       # Optimized assets from backup/
  scripts/
    migration/                    # WP -> MDX converter (from backup/)
```

---

## Design tokens (Tailwind v4)

Extract brand colors from current site backup, define in `app/globals.css`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  --color-brand-primary: /* extract from backup */;
  --color-brand-accent: /* CTA color, one accent only */;
  --color-surface: oklch(0.98 0 0);
  --color-text-primary: oklch(0.15 0 0);
  --font-sans: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;

  --radius-lg: 12px;

```

Reference: [obsidian/07-UX/Design-System.md](obsidian/07-UX/Design-System.md) for full token spec.

---

## Blog migration pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Backup["backup/metadata/api/posts-all.json"] --> Script["scripts/migration/wp-to-mdx.ts"]
    Script --> Clean["HTML cleanup + shortcode removal"]
    Clean --> Convert["Turndown HTML to Markdown"]
    Convert --> Frontmatter["gray-matter frontmatter"]
    Frontmatter --> MdxFiles["content/blog/{slug}.mdx"]
    MdxFiles --> Validate["Zod schema validation"]
    Validate --> RouteTest["Playwright: 328 URLs return 200"]
```

**Critical:** Slug in frontmatter must match `blog-inventory.json` exactly. No `/blog/` prefix.

Migration script packages: `turndown`, `gray-matter`, `cheerio` (HTML cleanup), `zod`.

---

## Performance and SEO requirements

| Requirement | Implementation |
|-------------|---------------|
| 328 blog URLs preserved | Catch-all `[slug]` route, static params from inventory |
| Core Web Vitals | SSG for marketing pages, `next/image` for all images |
| Schema markup | `schema-dts` per page type (see [Page-Templates.md](obsidian/07-UX/Page-Templates.md)) |
| Sitemap | `next-sitemap` auto-generate from routes + blog slugs |
| robots.txt | Allow all indexable, block /api/ |
| Font loading | `next/font` with `display: swap` |
| Motion performance | `will-change: transform` only on animated elements, `useReducedMotion` hook |
| Browser mockup images | WebP screenshots, lazy load below fold |

---

## Implementation phases

### Phase 2A: Scaffold and foundation (Week 1)
- `create-next-app` with TypeScript, Tailwind v4, App Router
- shadcn init + install core components
- Design tokens from backup brand colors
- `ContentRepository` interface + `JsonContentRepository`
- JSON config files for site, nav, homepage
- Header, footer, mega menu (from [Navigation-Footer-Spec.md](obsidian/07-UX/Navigation-Footer-Spec.md))

### Phase 2B: Browser mockup + homepage (Week 2)
- Build `BrowserMockup` component in-house
- Create tab content panels (PPC dashboard, listing SEO, account health)
- Assemble 12 homepage sections from JSON config
- Motion animations with reduced-motion support
- Homepage SEO metadata + FAQPage schema

### Phase 2C: Blog migration (Week 3-4)
- WP-to-MDX migration script from backup
- Catch-all blog route with static generation
- Blog template (TOC, FAQ, author box, related posts)
- Verify all 328 URLs with Playwright
- Sitemap generation

### Phase 2D: Service and utility pages (Week 5)
- Service page template (dedicated layout, Service schema)
- Case study index + detail pages
- Contact and free audit forms (Server Actions + Zod)
- About page

### Phase 2E: Polish and launch prep (Week 6)
- Lighthouse audit (target 90+ all categories)

Research complete — design system updated for a more enterprise, Amazon-style feel.

## Research findings

| Company | Typography approach | Button pattern |
|---------|---------------------|------------------|
| **Amazon** | Custom Ember (humanist sans) — one family for UI + headlines | Solid primary CTA; text links for tertiary |
| **Microsoft** | Aptos / Segoe — neutral, readable, no personality overload | Primary solid, secondary outline, tertiary = text link with underline on hover |
| **Apple** | SF Pro — single system font, weight-based hierarchy | Minimal buttons; links underline on hover |

**Fonts to avoid (AI-startup vibe):** Syne, Geist, Manrope, Plus Jakarta — overused on generic SaaS/AI sites.

**Enterprise B2B recommendation:** Single humanist sans family — **IBM Plex Sans** (IBM’s open-source font, similar intent to Amazon Ember / Microsoft Aptos).

---

## Changes made

### Typography
- **Before:** Syne (display) + Manrope (body) — trendy, AI-startup feel
- **After:** **IBM Plex Sans** only — headings + body, weights 400–700
- Slightly smaller, calmer type scale (display 44px instead of 48px bold)

### Colors (more enterprise, less playful)
- Text: `#0F1111` (Amazon-style near-black) instead of pure black
- Secondary text: `#565959` (Amazon gray)
- Borders: `#D5D9D9` (neutral, not bright)
- **Gold `#EAAB1D` kept** — your brand accent, used only for CTA hover and focus
- **Removed:** blue decorative shadow (`#162699`), extra orange highlights, multi-accent stats/icons

### Buttons
- **Ghost buttons removed**
- **New `link` variant:** transparent, underline on hover (Microsoft/Amazon pattern)
- Use for “Learn more”, “See all”, card tertiary actions

**Build error fix ho gaya** — `design-system.json` mein line 142 par trailing comma thi (`"animation": "lift-shadow-fill",`). Woh hata di.

**Accessibility aur responsiveness** bhi add ki:

### Accessibility
- **Skip to main content** link — Tab se page load par dikhega (`src/components/layout/skip-link.tsx`)
- **Viewport meta** — `device-width`, zoom up to 5x (`layout.tsx`)
- **Global `:focus-visible`** — accent ring sab interactive elements par
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`** — global CSS mein animations/transitions off
- **Fluid typography** — `clamp()` se headings scale hoti hain, body min 16px
- **Mobile section jump** — labeled `<select>` se 18 sections par jump (`design-system-mobile-nav.tsx`)
- **Section 17** updated — implemented vs planned list refresh

### Responsiveness
- **`container-page`** utility — `px-4 sm:px-6`, max-width 6xl
- **Header** — mobile par stack, badge wrap
- **Section padding** — `py-8` mobile, `py-12` desktop
- **Browser mockups** — macOS `overflow-x-auto`, iOS `max-w-md` centered; `xl:grid-cols-2` par side-by-side
- **Sidebar nav** — `lg+` only; mobile par jump select

### Verification
| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| JSON parse | Verified |
| TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`) | Verified |
| `npm run build` | Windows EISDIR error (env issue, pehle se tha — code se related nahi) |

- **375px** — mobile layout, section jump, iOS mockup
- **768px** — tablet grids
- **1280px** — sidebar + dual browser mockups

### Dark mode aur accessibility kaise check karein?

**Dark mode:** Abhi **build nahi hua** (Phase 1). DevTools → Rendering → `prefers-color-scheme: dark` se colors change nahi honge jab tak dark tokens na aayein.

| Test | Kaise |
|------|-------|
| Keyboard | Page reload → Tab dabao → Skip link dikhe → buttons/tabs par navigate |
| Lighthouse | F12 → Lighthouse → Accessibility → Analyze (target 90+) |
| axe | axe DevTools extension install → Scan page |
| Contrast | webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker — navy #0B1B3A, gold #EAAB1D |
| Reduced motion | Windows Settings → Accessibility → Animation effects Off |
| Responsive | Ctrl+Shift+M → 375px, 768px, 1280px test |
| Screen reader | NVDA (free) ya Windows Narrator (Win+Ctrl+Enter) |

# Tech Stack

**Status:** Verified (Phase 0 implementation + user approval P0-07, 2026-09-02)  
**Related:** [[System-Architecture]], [[Content-Architecture]], [[Folder-Structure]], [[Design-System]]

---

## Summary

Custom TypeScript Next.js application replacing ecomgliders.com. Content is JSON- and MDX-driven with a CMS-ready repository abstraction. Design tokens live in `content/config/design-system.json` and are approved via `/design-system`.

---

## Core stack

| Layer | Choice | Version (observed) | Why |
|-------|--------|-------------------|-----|
| Framework | Next.js (App Router) | 15.5.x | SSR/SSG/ISR for SEO, metadata API, image optimization, catch-all routes for 328 blog URLs |
| Language | TypeScript (strict) | 6.x | Type-safe config, components, Zod schemas |
| Runtime | React | 19.x | Server Components + client islands where needed |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 | 4.3.x | `@theme` tokens, design-system CSS variables, fast iteration |
| UI primitives | shadcn/ui (owned code) | Radix-based | Accessible primitives, no vendor lock-in, copied into repo |
| Validation | Zod | 4.x | JSON config schemas, form validation, content contracts |
| Animations | Motion (`motion/react`) | 13.x | PrimaryButton, ElegantCard — minimal in-house motion only |
| Icons | Lucide React | 1.x | Professional icons; no Unicode symbols as UI icons |
| Fonts | IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono | Google Fonts via `next/font` | Enterprise-readable single-family system (approved Phase 0) |

---

## Content and data

| Concern | Phase 1 choice | Future option |
|---------|----------------|---------------|
| Site config | `content/config/*.json` | Keystatic or Payload via adapter |
| Blog posts | MDX in `content/blog/` | Same adapter swap |
| Design tokens | `content/config/design-system.json` | Unchanged — source of truth |
| Blog URL inventory | `backup/metadata/blog-inventory.json` | Migration reference only |
| Database | None (file-based) | Optional if CMS requires it later |

**Pattern:** Repository + Adapter — UI and services depend on `ContentRepository` interface, not file format.

---

## SEO and metadata

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `next/metadata` | Per-page title, description, robots, Open Graph |
| `schema-dts` (planned P2+) | FAQPage, Organization, Service structured data |
| `docs/seo/SITE-SEO-MAP.md` | Indexable page SEO records (required per page) |
| Identical blog paths | Catch-all `app/[slug]/page.tsx` — no URL changes without documented 301 |

---

## Forms (planned P3-07)

| Layer | Choice |
|-------|--------|
| Client | React Hook Form |
| Validation | Zod (shared schemas server + client) |
| Submit | Next.js Server Actions |
| Security | Server-side validation, CSRF on state-changing requests |

Not yet installed — add when contact/audit forms are implemented.

---

## Testing and quality

| Tool | Status |
|------|--------|
| TypeScript `tsc --noEmit` | Verified — passes |
| ESLint + eslint-config-next | Installed; `next lint` deprecated in Next.js 16 |
| Playwright (MCP) | Used for site audit and `/design-system` verification |
| axe-core / Lighthouse | Planned P4-02, P4-03 |

---

## Deployment (proposed)

| Item | Choice | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| Hosting | Vercel | Native Next.js, preview deploys, ISR |
| CI | TBD | Lint + typecheck on PR |
| Staging | Vercel preview URL | P4-04 |

Requires confirmation before production cutover.

---

## Explicitly not used

| Rejected | Reason |
|----------|--------|
| Framer.com export as production code | Poor SEO control, not maintainable |
| Paid block libraries (Tailark Pro, Aceternity Pro) | Build custom in-house per brand |
| Astro | Weaker for interactive components + future admin in same app |
| Plain React SPA | SEO penalty for 328 indexed posts |
| WordPress (current platform) | Migration target is custom code |
| Heavy Framer motion effects | Rejected in Phase 0 — enterprise positioning |

---

## Repository layout (application)

```
src/
├── app/                    # Next.js App Router pages
├── components/
│   ├── ui/                 # shadcn primitives + PrimaryButton, ElegantCard
│   ├── layout/             # Header, footer, skip link (P1-07+)
│   ├── sections/           # Homepage sections (P2-03+)
│   ├── browser-mockup/     # Static browser chrome (Phase 0)
│   └── design-system/      # /design-system review page
├── domain/                 # ContentRepository, services (P1-06+)
├── infrastructure/         # JsonFileAdapter, MdxAdapter (P1-06+)
└── lib/
    ├── design-tokens.ts    # Zod + CSS variable builder
    ├── content-config.ts   # browser-mockup + review page config
    └── icon-registry.ts    # Lucide name → component map

content/
├── config/                 # JSON site content (design-system, site, nav, homepage)
└── blog/                   # MDX posts (P3-01+)
```

---

## Environment and secrets

- Secrets via environment variables only — never in source, JSON, or client bundles
- `.env.local` for local dev (gitignored)
- Vercel environment variables for staging/production

---

## Version policy

- Pin major versions in `package.json`; review before major upgrades
- Next.js 15 LTS line until Phase 4 launch verified
- New dependencies: verify maintenance, license, bundle impact per cookbook Section 55

---

## Decision record

Formal stack decision logged in `docs/project/DECISIONS.md` under P1-04 (Q3).

# Browser Mockup Specification **Status:** Verified (Phase 0 static implementation, P0-07 approved 2026-09-02) **Related:** [[Design-System]], [[Page-Templates]], [[Content-Architecture]], [[Design-Inspiration]] --- ## Purpose Reusable in-house browser chrome component that displays Amazon Seller Central-style dashboard previews inside macOS or iOS Safari frames. Used on homepage hero, service pages, case studies, and `/design-system` section 13. **Not a third-party dependency.** Built from design tokens and JSON config — no iframe, no external mockup library. --- ## Design decision (approved) | Mode | Status | Rationale | |------|--------|-----------| | **Static preview** | **Active (Phase 0)** | Fixed tab per variant; decorative chrome; no click/hover/auto-rotate. Avoids user confusion on review and marketing pages. | | Interactive tabs | Deferred | Optional future enhancement via `staticPreview: false` in config. Requires explicit approval before enabling on production pages. | | Auto-rotate | Rejected for Phase 0 | Distracting; paused-on-hover complexity not needed for agency positioning. | --- ## Component location ``` src/components/browser-mockup/ browser-mockup.tsx # Main export — chrome + layout browser-mockup-content.tsx # Stats grid + table panel browser-mockup-chart.tsx # Static SVG area chart browser-mockup-data.ts # Re-exports from content-config (deprecated direct use) index.ts # Public API content/config/browser-mockup.json # All tab data, variant defaults, copy src/lib/content-config.ts # Zod schema + loaders ``` --- ## Public API ### Export ```typescript // src/components/browser-mockup/index.ts export { BrowserMockup } from "./browser-mockup"; export type { BrowserVariant } from "./browser-mockup-data"; ``` ### BrowserMockupProps ```typescript interface BrowserMockupProps { /** Additional Tailwind classes on the figure wrapper */ className?: string; /** Browser chrome variant. Default: "macos" */ variant?: BrowserVariant; /** Optional figcaption above the frame (e.g. "macOS Desktop") */ label?: string; } type BrowserVariant = "macos" | "ios"; ``` ### Usage ```tsx import { BrowserMockup } from "@/components/browser-mockup"; // Desktop — shows PPC Dashboard tab (from config) // Mobile — shows Account Analytics tab (from config)
``` **Config keys:** `components.browserMockup` in `design-system.json`; data in `browser-mockup.json`. --- ## Variants | Variant | Frame | Chrome | Default tab | Content density | |---------|-------|--------|-------------|-----------------| | `macos` | `rounded-xl`, full width | Traffic lights + nav buttons + tab bar + URL bar | `ppc` | Standard padding | | `ios` | `rounded-[2rem]`, max-w-md | Status bar + Dynamic Island + Safari bar + segmented tabs | `analytics` | Compact (`compact={true}`) | Default tab per variant is set in `browser-mockup.json`: ```json { "defaultTabByVariant": { "macos": "ppc", "ios": "analytics" } } ``` --- ## Config schema **File:** `content/config/browser-mockup.json` **Validator:** `browserMockupConfigSchema` in `src/lib/content-config.ts` ### Root fields | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `defaultTabByVariant` | `{ macos: string, ios: string }` | Tab `id` shown per variant | | `previewDescription` | `string` | Copy on `/design-system` section 13 | | `variants` | `Record` | Figcaption labels | | `tabs` | `BrowserTab[]` | Full tab definitions | ### BrowserTab ```typescript interface BrowserTab { id: string; // "ppc" | "seo" | "analytics" label: string; // Full tab label (macOS bar) shortLabel: string; // Abbreviated (iOS segmented control) url: string; // URL bar text (no protocol) chartLabel: string; // Chart header stats: { label: string; value: string; progress: number; // 0–100, progress bar width }[]; chart: number[]; // Normalized values for SVG path chartPoints: { label: string; // X-axis label value: string; // Display value (header badge) raw: number; // Numeric for path calculation }[]; table: { label: string; value: string; change: string; positive?: boolean; // true = success color, false = error detail?: string; // Reserved for expandable rows (not used in static mode) }[]; } ``` ### Built-in tabs (Phase 0) | id | label | url | Use case | |----|-------|-----|----------| | `ppc` | PPC Dashboard | sellercentral.amazon.com/ppc/campaigns | macOS default — ad performance | | `seo` | Listing SEO | sellercentral.amazon.com/listing/optimizer | Listing optimization | | `analytics` | Account Analytics | sellercentral.amazon.com/analytics/overview | iOS default — revenue overview | **To change any value:** edit `browser-mockup.json` only — no component changes required. --- ## Subcomponents (internal) | Component | File | Responsibility | |-----------|------|----------------| | `BrowserMockup` | `browser-mockup.tsx` | Figure wrapper, variant routing, chrome assembly | | `MacChrome` | `browser-mockup.tsx` | Traffic lights, back/forward/refresh, tab bar, URL bar | | `IosChrome` | `browser-mockup.tsx` | Status bar, Safari controls, segmented tabs | | `StaticTabBar` | `browser-mockup.tsx` | Decorative tabs (`aria-hidden="true"`) | | `BrowserMockupContent` | `browser-mockup-content.tsx` | Chart + 3 stat cards + data table | | `BrowserMockupChart` | `browser-mockup-chart.tsx` | Static SVG line/area chart, last point in header | --- ## Visual specification ### Design tokens (from `design-system.json`) | Element | Token | |---------|-------| | Frame border | `border-border` | | macOS chrome bg | `bg-surface-muted` | | iOS frame | `bg-surface`, `rounded-[2rem]` | | Active tab | `ring-accent/15` or `ring-accent/20` | | Chart accent | `var(--color-accent)` gradient | | Stat card top border | `border-t-accent`, `border-t-brand-cyan`, `border-t-primary` (rotating) | | Positive change | `text-success` | | Negative change | `text-error` | | URL lock icon | `text-success` (macOS), `text-text-secondary` (iOS) | ### macOS traffic lights System chrome colors only (not brand tokens): `#FF5F57`, `#FFBD2E`, `#28C840`. ### Chart - Static SVG — no hover, tooltip, or touch handlers - Shows last data point value in header badge - Subtle accent glow via `feDropShadow` filter - `role="img"` with `aria-label` describing chart label and last value --- ## **P1-06 complete.** The content layer abstraction is in place per `Content-Architecture.md`.

### Architecture

```
ContentRepository (interface)
    └── CompositeContentRepository
            ├── JsonFileContentRepository  → content/config/*.json
            └── MdxBlogRepository (stub)   → content/blog/*.mdx (P3-01)
```

### Created

| Layer | Files |
|-------|-------|
| Domain | `content-repository.ts`, `errors.ts`, schemas for homepage, FAQ, service, case study, testimonial, blog, page SEO |
| Infrastructure | `json-file-content-repository.ts`, `mdx-blog-repository.ts`, `composite-content-repository.ts`, `create-content-repository.ts`, `get-content-repository.ts` |

### Behavior

- **Required files** (`site.json`, `navigation.json`) — load and validate via Zod; throw `ContentValidationError` on schema mismatch
- **Optional files** (`homepage.json`, `testimonials.json`, `faq.json`, `case-studies.json`, `services/{slug}.json`) — return `null` / `[]` when missing
- **Blog** — `MdxBlogRepository` stub returns `null` / `[]` until P3-01
- **Caching** — in-memory cache keyed by file mtime (re-reads when file changes in dev)
- **Server usage** — `getContentRepository()` wrapped in React `cache()` for per-request singleton

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — pass
- Runtime: site "eCom Gliders", 5 nav items; `getHomepage()` throws `ContentNotFoundError` (expected — `homepage.json` is P2-02)

import { z } from "zod";

export const contactFormSchema = z.object({
  name: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .min(2, "Enter your full name.")
    .max(100, "Name must be 100 characters or fewer."),
  email: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .email("Enter a valid email address.")
    .max(254, "Email must be 254 characters or fewer."),
  phone: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .min(7, "Enter a valid phone number.")
    .max(30, "Phone number must be 30 characters or fewer."),
  serviceInterest: z.string().trim().max(100).optional(),
  message: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .min(10, "Message must be at least 10 characters.")
    .max(5000, "Message must be 5000 characters or fewer."),
  consent: z.literal("true", {
    errorMap: () => ({ message: "You must agree to the privacy policy." }),
  }),
  website: z.string().max(0).optional(),
});

export type ContactFormInput = z.infer<typeof contactFormSchema>;

import { z } from "zod";

export const auditFormSchema = z.object({
  name: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .min(2, "Enter your full name.")
    .max(100, "Name must be 100 characters or fewer."),
  email: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .email("Enter a valid email address.")
    .max(254, "Email must be 254 characters or fewer."),
  phone: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .min(7, "Enter a valid phone number.")
    .max(30, "Phone number must be 30 characters or fewer."),
  brandName: z.string().trim().min(1).max(150).optional(),
  amazonStoreUrl: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .url("Enter a valid Amazon store URL.")
    .max(500)
    .optional()
    .or(z.literal("")),
  monthlyRevenue: z.string().trim().max(50).optional(),
  message: z.string().trim().max(5000).optional(),
  consent: z.literal("true", {
    errorMap: () => ({ message: "You must agree to the privacy policy." }),
  }),
  website: z.string().max(0).optional(),
});

export type AuditFormInput = z.infer<typeof auditFormSchema>;

# Google Search Console — Sitemap Submission

**Task:** P4-05  
**Updated:** 2026-09-02

---

## Sitemap URLs

| Environment | Property URL | Sitemap to submit |
|---------------|--------------|-------------------|
| Staging (now) | `https://ecom-gliders.vercel.app` | `https://ecom-gliders.vercel.app/sitemap.xml` |
| Production (cutover) | `https://ecomgliders.com` | `https://ecomgliders.com/sitemap.xml` |

Submit only after the Search Console property matches the live site URL.

---

## Pre-submission checklist (automated)

Run:

```bash
npm run verify:gsc-readiness
# Staging default; or:
npm run verify:gsc-readiness -- https://ecomgliders.com
```

Report: `docs/qa/search-console-readiness.json`

Requirements:

- [ ] `/robots.txt` HTTP 200 and references sitemap
- [ ] `/sitemap.xml` HTTP 200, valid urlset, 340+ URLs
- [ ] Sitemap `<loc>` host matches the property URL
- [ ] Property verified in Google Search Console

---

## Manual submission steps

1. Open [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console).
2. Select or add the property (Domain or URL prefix).
   - Staging: URL prefix `https://ecom-gliders.vercel.app`
   - Production: Domain `ecomgliders.com` (recommended) or URL prefix `https://ecomgliders.com`
3. Go to **Sitemaps** in the left menu.
4. Enter `sitemap.xml` (or the full sitemap URL).
5. Click **Submit**.
6. Confirm status shows **Success** (may take minutes to hours for first fetch).

---

## Production cutover

Before submitting `https://ecomgliders.com/sitemap.xml`:

1. Point DNS to Vercel (or hosting).
2. Set Vercel env `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://ecomgliders.com`.

**Multi-level meaning for this project:** Level 1 = Services trigger → Level 2 = named categories → Level 3 = individual services with title + outcome description. Not nested flyout menus (those feel dated). Wide categorized panel is the boutique standard.

## Detailed research: Apple / Amazon idea vs our case

### What Apple does (idea only)

[Apple.com](https://www.apple.com) puts **product lines as top nav tabs**, and **each tab opens its own mega menu**:

- Top tabs: Store, Mac, iPad, iPhone, Watch, AirPods, TV & Home, Entertainment, Accessories, Support
- Inside each mega: left column “Explore [Product]” + right “Shop [Product]” / quick links / support

**Why that works for Apple:** thousands of SKUs, shoppers already think in product names (iPhone, Mac).

**Why we do NOT copy that literally:** eCom Gliders is a **services agency**, not a product catalog. Putting “PPC”, “Listing”, “Trademark” as separate top tabs would make the header noisy and look like a SaaS product strip — not a premium Amazon partner.

### What Amazon does (idea only)

Amazon uses a **Departments / All** mega + many department categories (Electronics, Fashion, etc.) optimized for browsing millions of products.

**Why we do NOT copy that:** seller buyers come with a **problem** (ACOS, ranking, Brand Registry), not a department name. A retail-department menu would feel wrong for B2B agency trust.

### What boutique Amazon agencies do (our real peer set)

From project research ([Competitor-Analysis](obsidian/09-Research/Competitor-Analysis.md), COMPETITIVE-RESEARCH):

| Agency | Mega pattern | Takeaway |
|--------|--------------|----------|
| Olifant | **One** Services mega + CTA panel | Best structural fit |
| Sequence | Multi-level services mega + Free audit | Category depth OK |
| Canopy / MAG | Simple dropdown or light mega | Clean, not childish |
| AMZ Dudes | No mega — horizontal + CTA | Conversion, less IA |

**eCom Gliders decision:** Apple’s *clarity of grouping* + Olifant’s *one Services mega + CTA* — not Apple’s many top-level megas.

### Critical distinction: header tabs vs mega categories

Two different things people call “tabs”:

1. **Header tabs** = items in the top bar (Services, Case Studies, …)
2. **Mega categories** = columns *inside* the Services panel (Advertising & Growth, …)

**Only ONE header tab gets a mega menu: Services.**  
All other header tabs are simple links (cleaner, more premium, less confusing).

```
HEADER TABS (top bar)
├── Services          ← ONLY this opens MEGA MENU
├── Case Studies      ← simple link
├── About             ← simple link
├── Blog              ← simple link
├── Contact           ← simple link
└── [Free Audit]      ← CTA button (not a mega)

INSIDE Services MEGA (category columns — like Apple’s inner groups)
├── Advertising & Growth
├── Catalog & Content
├── Brand & Operations
└── CTA rail (audit + phone + metric)
```

## Target information architecture

### Header tabs — final list

[Logo]  Services▾  Case Studies  About  Blog  Contact     [Free Audit]

| Case Studies | Link `/case-studies/` | Proof, not a service list |
| About | Link `/about-us/` | Trust / team |
| Blog | Link `/blog/` | 328 posts — keep visible (competitor gap we already fixed) |
| Contact | Link `/contact/` | Direct path |
| Free Audit | CTA button | Always visible conversion (industry standard) |

**Not in header (intentional):** Home, Testimonials, Who We Are, Resources mega, Industries mega — folds into About / Case Studies / Blog.

### Services mega — 3 category columns + CTA (this is the “detailed” part)

```
┌─ Advertising & Growth ─┬─ Catalog & Content ───┬─ Brand & Operations ──┬─ CTA ────────┐
│ ★ Account Management   │ Listing Opt + SEO     │ Trademark + Registry  │ Free audit   │
│   PPC Management       │ Content Writing       │ Company Registration  │ $112M+ proof │
│   Amazon DSP           │ Visual Creativity     │ Website SEO + Dev     │ phone        │
│   Reporting            │ Catalog Management    │ Product Sourcing      │              │
└────────────────────────┴───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┴──────────────┘
                         [ View all services → ]
```

#### Column 1 — Advertising & Growth

Buyer intent: “Grow sales / fix ads / manage account.”

| Service | Role in menu | Outcome-style description (direction) |
|---------|--------------|----------------------------------------|
| Amazon Account Management | **Featured / flagship** | Full-service growth with dedicated in-house managers |
| PPC Management | Core money driver | Sponsored Products, Brands, Display — ACOS control |
| Amazon DSP | Advanced ads | Upper-funnel and retargeting beyond SP/SB |

#### Column 2 — Catalog & Content

| Content Writing | Core | Titles, bullets, A+, brand story |

#### Column 3 — Brand & Operations

Buyer intent: “Set up / protect brand / ops support.”

| Company Registration | Setup | US entity for sellers |

# Navigation and Footer Specification

**Research date:** 2026-09-02  
**Updated:** 2026-09-02  
**Status:** Approved (implemented in `content/config/navigation.json`)  
**Related:** [[Design-Inspiration]], [[Page-Templates]], [[Competitor-Analysis]]

---

## Purpose

Complete specification for eCom Gliders header, mega menu, mobile navigation, and footer on the new custom site.

---

## Design principles

1. Single navigation system (no duplicates)
2. Header CTA always visible
3. Dedicated page URLs for all service links (no anchor hashes)
4. Logo links to homepage (no "Home" nav item)
5. Mobile-first responsive behavior
6. WCAG AA accessibility minimum
7. Amazon remains the brand hero; multi-channel lives in a dedicated mega column

---

## Header structure

### Desktop layout

```
[Announcement bar - Verified Partner | $112M+ | 95% retention]
[Logo]  Services v  |  Case Studies  |  About  |  Blog  |  Contact  |  [Free Audit button]
```

### Top announcement bar (enabled)

```
Rated Amazon Ads Verified Partner | $112M+ revenue managed | 95% client retention
```

- Full-width strip above main header
- Link to case studies
- Config: `site.json` → `announcementBar.enabled: true`

### Main header

| Element | Specification |
|---------|---------------|
| Logo | Left-aligned, links to `/` |
| Nav items | Services (mega), Case Studies, About, Blog, Contact |
| CTA button | Free Audit → `/free-audit-2/` |
| Sticky | Yes |
| Only one mega | Services |

---

## Mega menu specification

### Trigger

- Nav item: Services
- Opens on hover (desktop) or accordion (mobile)
- Full-width panel below header (`max-w-7xl` inner)

### Layout (4 service columns + CTA rail)

```
Advertising and Growth | Catalog and Content | Brand and Operations | Channels and DTC | CTA
```

Levels:

1. Header: Services
2. Category column titles
3. Individual services with icon, title, outcome description

### Column 1 — Advertising and Growth

| Service | URL | Notes |
|---------|-----|-------|
| Amazon Account Management | `/full-service-amazon-agency/` | Featured / Flagship |
| Amazon PPC Management | `/amazon-ppc-management-agency/` | Live page |
| Amazon DSP | `/amazon-dsp-management/` | Proposed page |
| Reporting and Analytics | `/amazon-reporting-analytics/` | Proposed page |

### Column 2 — Catalog and Content

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Listing Optimization and SEO | `/amazon-listing-optimization/` |
| Content Writing | `/amazon-content-writing/` |
| Visual Creativity | `/amazon-visual-creativity/` |
| Video Creative | `/amazon-video-creative/` |
| Catalog Management | `/amazon-catalog-management/` |

### Column 3 — Brand and Operations

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Trademark and Brand Registry | `/amazon-trademark-brand-registry/` |
| Company Registration | `/amazon-company-registration/` |
| Product Sourcing | `/amazon-product-sourcing/` |

### Column 4 — Channels and DTC

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Shopify and Website Development | `/shopify-website-development/` |
| TikTok Shop Ads | `/tiktok-shop-ads/` |
| Email and Retention Marketing | `/email-retention-marketing/` |

### CTA rail

- Eyebrow: Amazon Ads Verified Partner
- Metric: $112M+ revenue managed
- Title: Free Amazon account audit
- Button: Get Free Audit (accent on primary panel)
- Phone: +1 (360) 660-1210

### Panel footer

- View all services → `/full-service-amazon-agency/`

### Backlog (not in mega v1)

Walmart Marketplace, Meta Ads, Google Shopping — add only after delivery confirmation.

---

## Mobile navigation

- Sheet drawer from right
- Services accordion with four category sections
- Link descriptions + flagship label visible
- Free Audit + phone + email in drawer footer

---

## Footer

Four columns: Brand | Services (flagship Amazon + Channels highlights) | Company | Contact  
Legal: Privacy Policy, Terms and Conditions

---

- [`content/config/navigation.json`](../../content/config/navigation.json)
- Schema: `src/domain/content/schemas/navigation.schema.ts`
- UI: `src/components/layout/mega-menu-panel.tsx`, `nav-link-item.tsx`, `mobile-nav.tsx`

content.text:
## Services: Fiverr vs badi agencies vs tumhara menu

### Fiverr pe kya milta hai (Observed)
Fiverr pe mostly **VA / gig bundles** hain, agency playbook nahi:

- Account management / Seller Central VA  
- Listing + keyword SEO  
- PPC (SP/SB/SD)  
- A+ / Brand Registry help  
- Inventory / suppressed listings / flat files  

Yeh **task list** lagti hai. Professional agency is se alag dikhti hai kyunki woh **capability systems** bechti hai, “I will do X” nahi.

### Badi ecommerce agencies (2026) — common professional stack
Sources: [Eva](https://eva.guru/), [Canopy / Velocity / Trivium summaries](https://sellerplex.com/best-amazon-agencies/), [Sequence](https://sequencecommerce.com/amazon/), [Shaazford industries](https://amazonagency.shaazford.com/industries)

| Layer | Typical services |
|--------|------------------|
| **Core Amazon** | Full account management, PPC, listing SEO, A+/creative, catalog, reporting |
| **Advanced ads** | DSP, AMC (jab capability ho) |
| **Ops / brand** | Brand Registry, account health, sometimes sourcing / inventory advisory |
| **Channels** | Shopify/DTC, TikTok Shop, Walmart (peers ab yeh dikhate hain) |
| **Usually NOT in primary nav as equal pillars** | Random Fiverr-style “flat file”, “giveaways”, “patent” dumps |

### Tumhara current mega (already strong direction)
Advertising | Catalog & Content | Brand & Ops | Channels & DTC — yeh **agency-grade** hai, Fiverr dump nahi.

**Professional lagane ke liye rules (recommendation):**
1. **Amazon hero** rakho (brand truth: Verified Partner, $112M+, Amazon-first).  
2. Shopify / TikTok **Channels** column mein theek hain — sirf tab jab deliver kar sakte ho; warna “Coming” / hide.  
3. Nav mein **Walmart / Meta / Google** abhi backlog — peers ke paas hain, lekin empty promise amateur dikhta hai.  
4. Mega mein **short outcome lines**, Fiverr-style 15-bullet VA lists nahi.  
5. Missing pages (404 links) professional feel kill karti hain — pehle pages ya links trim.

**Optional adds (sirf jab real delivery ho):** Brand Store / A+ as explicit line under Catalog; Account Health under Brand/Ops; Inventory advisory under Account Mgmt copy — alag mega items zaroori nahi.

---

## Industries / “Who we work with” — chahiye ya nahi?

Do alag cheezein hain:

| Type | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| **Buyer stage** (“Who we serve”) | New seller / scaling / multi-ASIN | Tumhare homepage pe **already hai** |
| **Product vertical / Industries** | Home & Kitchen, Supplements, Beauty, Pets… | Sequence / Shaazford jaisi sites |

### Research-backed verdict

**Alag full `/industries/` page abhi unnecessary hai** eCom Gliders ke liye — agar tumhare paas:

- har vertical ke liye dedicated playbooks / case studies / content depth nahi  
- nav pe pehle se Services + Case Studies + Blog busy hai  

**Kyun peers industries dikhate hain:** enterprise SEO + “hum is category ke specialist hain” signal. Boutique Tier B (Olifant-style target) ke liye yeh **nice-to-have**, blocker nahi.

**Kya rakho (recommended, lean):**

1. **Homepage “Who we serve”** — stage-based (jo ab hai) — **rakhna**. Yeh industries nahi, buyer fit hai.  
2. **Case studies pe category filters** (Kitchen, Sports, etc.) — industries ka kaam case studies se ho jata hai, bina alag page ke.  
3. **Alag Industries mega / nav item** — **ab mat add karo** (clutter + thin content risk).  
4. Baad mein (Phase 2+) — agar 4–6 strong vertical case studies + blog clusters hon, tab `/industries/` ya homepage pe chhota “Categories we scale” strip.

**Unnecessary kab hota hai:** sirf “Home & Kitchen, Beauty, Electronics…” cards bina proof / bina pages ke — yeh AI-agency filler lagta hai.

---

## Short answer

| Sawal | Answer |
|--------|--------|
| Fiverr jaisi services list? | Nahi — Fiverr = VA tasks. Tum = capability columns (jo direction sahi hai). |
| Big ecom se kya seekhein? | Amazon core + DSP/reporting + creative; channels (Shopify/TikTok) secondary; sirf delivered services. |
| Industries page? | **Abhi nahi.** Homepage Who we serve + case study categories kaafi. Full industries page later, jab proof ho. |

Agar chaho to Agent mode mein next step: mega se undelivered items trim + homepage Who we serve copy tighten (industries add kiye baghair).

Best path yeh hai — **Amazon-first agency**, complete dikhe, lekin empty promises / Fiverr dump / unnecessary industries page se bachna.

## Non-negotiable (miss mat karna)

### 1. Services (mega + real pages)
**Rakho (professional core):**
- Account Management (flagship)
- PPC
- Listing SEO
- Content + Visual + Video
- Catalog
- Reporting
- Brand Registry / Trademark
- Company Registration (purani site pe tha)
- Product Sourcing (purani site pe tha)
- DSP (agar deliver hota hai)

**Channels (secondary, delivery confirm ke saath):**
- Shopify & Website
- TikTok Shop Ads
- Email / Retention

**Abhi nav mein mat daalo (miss nahi — backlog):**
- Walmart, Meta, Google — tab jab team ready ho

**Sab se bada miss risk:** mega links ka **404** — professional kill karta hai. Ya page banao, ya link hatao / “Contact for X” rakho.

### 2. Trust (already strong — mat todna)
- Amazon Ads Verified Partner
- $112M+ / 95% / since 2018 (sirf verified claims)
- Case studies with metrics
- Free Audit CTA har jagah clear

### 3. “Who we serve” vs Industries
| Cheez | Best decision |
|--------|----------------|
| Homepage **Who we serve** (new / scaling / multi-ASIN) | **Rakhna** — buyer stage, zaroori |
| Alag **Industries** page / nav item | **Abhi nahi** — thin content = amateur |
| Case studies pe categories | **Kaafi** — kitchen, sports, etc. yahan dikhao |

Industries baad mein jab 4–6 solid vertical proofs hon.

### 4. Site structure jo complete lage (bina clutter)
Nav: **Services | Case Studies | About | Blog | Contact | Free Audit**  
(Case Studies + Blog mega OK agar slim rahen)

Footer: Services highlights + Company + Contact + legal

### 5. SEO / migration (project non-negotiable)
- 328 blog URLs same
- Har indexable page pe SEO record
- Sitemap / staging pehle se ready; GSC submit user pe

---

## Priority order (best sequence)

1. **Mega polish locked** — compact, centered, underline nav (ho chuka direction)  
2. **Service pages** for every live mega link (ya links trim) — **sab se important miss-prevention**  
3. Homepage trust + Who we serve + case studies (industries page skip)  
4. Legal pages if linked (privacy/terms)  
5. Channels pages only after delivery confirm  
6. Optional later: Industries strip/page, Walmart, etc.

---

## One-line verdict

**Best = Amazon core complete + proof (cases/trust) + stage-based “Who we serve” + Channels only if real.**  
**Miss mat karo = service pages + honest claims.**  
**Skip abhi = full Industries hub + undelivered marketplaces.**

Agent mode mein bolo to isi checklist pe implement / gap-audit kar sakta hoon (kaun se mega links abhi 404 hain, kya pehle banana hai).

**Short answer:** 3rd-level hierarchy mega menu mein **mat daalo** — clarity badhne ke bajaye site complex aur “busy” feel karegi.

## Kyun risky hai

Tumhara Services mega pehle se **4 columns + CTA** hai. Uske upar nested 3rd level (expand/flyout) se:

- Desktop pe hover hell (miss-clicks, accidental closes)
- Mobile pe accordion ke andar accordion — confusing
- Pehle tumne khud kaha mega **bohot bada** lag raha tha — nesting usse worse karegi
- Clients “clearity” ke liye depth nahi, **seedha jawab** chahte hain

Industry-grade Amazon agencies usually **max 2 levels** rakhti hain: category → service page. 3rd level rare hai, aur tab bhi alag page pe, mega ke andar nahi.

## Better clarity (bina over-complexity)

| Approach | Complexity | Clarity |
|----------|------------|---------|
| Mega: category → service (abhi jaisa) | Low | Good |
| Service page pe **What’s included** / sub-sections | Low | Best |
| Optional “Related services” on page | Low | Good |
| 3rd-level mega flyouts | High | Weak |

Matlab: extra cheezein **service page ke andar** rakho (deliverables, process, FAQ) — nav mein nahi.

## Rule of thumb

- Nav / mega = **kahaan jana hai** (max ~12–15 links, grouped)
- Page = **kya milta hai** (detail, sub-offers, packages)

Agar kisi service ke under 4–5 sub-offers hain (e.g. PPC → Sponsored Products / Brands / Display), unhe **us page ke H2s** banao, mega mein 3rd level nahi.

**Verdict:** 3rd-level hierarchy se website over-complex ho jayegi. Clarity ke liye page depth badhao, menu depth nahi.

# Header Nav, Ribbon Bar, and CTA Research

**Date:** 2026-09-02  
**Method:** Live Playwright inspection + existing `docs/seo/COMPETITIVE-RESEARCH.md` / Competitor-Analysis  
**Confidence:** High for nav labels observed; Medium for conversion lift of any single pattern

---

## QUESTION

1. Which primary nav tabs do Tier A–C Amazon agencies use that eCom Gliders may be missing?
2. What makes a professional announcement / ribbon bar?
3. How do competitors style the header CTA (vs our navy “Free Audit” block)?

---

## EVIDENCE — Nav tabs (Observed 2026-09-02)

| Agency | Primary nav pattern | Header CTA |
|--------|---------------------|------------|
| Olifant Digital | Services mega (Amazon Services…), Case Studies, Tools | “Free Marketing Plan” (text + underline, not solid box) |
| Sequence Commerce | Solutions mega, Marketplaces, deep channel links | “Get a free audit” / “Book a strategy call” |
| Canopy Management | Services, The Team, The Tech, The Results, Resources | “Get In Touch” / free audit |
| My Amazon Guy | Resources hub (News, Articles, Webinars), Careers, Partnership | “Free Audit” / account audit |
| AMZ Dudes | Large Services mega only (Account, Marketing, Design…) | “Get my audit” |
| SalesDuo | Services, Solutions, Resources (Customers, Cases, Blog, About) | “Book Your 1:1 Growth Call” |

**eCom Gliders today:** Services · Case Studies · About · Blog · Contact + Free Audit

### Tabs often present elsewhere, missing for us

| Tab / pattern | Who has it | Add now? | Why |
|---------------|------------|----------|-----|
| Resources hub | Canopy, MAG, SalesDuo, Sequence | Later | Needs landing page grouping Blog + tools; Blog already in nav |
| Tools / calculators | Olifant, Sequence | Later | No live tools yet; empty tab hurts trust |
| The Team (top-level) | Canopy | No | Covered by About; avoid nav bloat |
| The Results | Canopy | No | Case Studies already covers |
| Solutions (separate from Services) | Sequence, SalesDuo | No | Duplicates Services mega for our scale |
| Careers / Events | MAG | No | No career/events product yet |
| Phone in header (utility) | AMZ Dudes, many mid-market | Yes (utility) | Conversion path without new page |
| Ask AI strip | AMZ Dudes | No | Novelty; not our brand |

**Conclusion (nav):** Current 5 items + CTA is aligned with Tier B “5–7 items max” (`Niche-Website-Standards`). Do **not** add Resources/Tools/Solutions until pages exist. Highest-value gap: **desktop phone link** beside CTA, not another tab.

---

## EVIDENCE — Ribbon / announcement bar

| Agency | Pattern | Takeaway |
|--------|---------|----------|
| Olifant | One line: rating · revenue metric · “See client results →” | Single sentence, middot separators, arrow link — not pipe soup |
| Sequence | Awards strip above nav | Social proof strip is expected at Tier A |
| eCom Gliders | Three claims + `\|` + “View case studies” | Correct content; separators and CTA affordance can match Olifant |

**Conclusion (ribbon):** Keep Verified Partner + $112M+ + 95%. Replace pipe separators with middots; lead with BadgeCheck icon (lucide); make case-studies link use ArrowRight — no emoji (project rule).

---

## EVIDENCE — Header CTA styling

| Pattern | Agencies | Look |
|---------|----------|------|
| Text / underline CTA | Olifant | Premium, not “blocky” |
| Filled high-contrast CTA | AMZ Dudes, SalesDuo, Canopy | Conversion-first |
| eCom Gliders | Solid navy PrimaryButton | Matches logo navy → CTA does not stand out; reads as a heavy box |

Design system already documents secondary as underline-text (Amazon/Microsoft/Apple) and primary as navy with accent hover. For **header conversion CTA**, industry mid-market uses a distinct accent fill so the action is not confused with chrome.

**Conclusion (CTA):** Header Free Audit → accent fill + lucide `ArrowRight` + refined padding. Keep navy primary for forms/secondary bands where brand weight matters.

---

- Announcement bar: BadgeCheck, middot separators, ArrowRight on link
- Optional desktop phone with Phone icon beside CTA

## NOT IMPLEMENTED (requires content)

- Resources top-level tab
- Tools tab
- Solutions rename

# Homepage Hero Redesign (30+ buyers)

## Scope lock

- **In scope:** Homepage hero section only (landing page first; rest of homepage later).
- **Out of scope:** Trust bar / stats / other sections (already exist below; only tighten how hero hands off to them). Mobile nav stays as-is.

## Audience and tone (30+)

Buyers are mid-career Amazon brand operators (scaling FBA / multi-ASIN). They reward:

- Clear outcome in one glance
- Credible proof without hype
- Calm product UI, not playful marketing chrome
- Direct CTA with low cognitive load

Avoid: emoji, decorative Unicode, “AI magic”, stacked mockups that feel busy, dark enterprise Canopy hero, youth-oriented motion noise.

## Research synthesis (Verified / Observed)

| Source | Takeaway for our hero |
|--------|------------------------|
| Olifant (Tier B) | Split: outcome copy left, trust/product right; application-style CTA |
| AMZ Dudes (Tier C) | Strong CTA urgency; stats live *below* hero (already Section 3) |
| Canopy / Sequence | Outcome H1 + single CTA; **skip** dark full-bleed enterprise hero |
| Cursor.com (Observed) | Short confident H1; product is the visual hero; one primary CTA; restrained whitespace; no clutter in first viewport |
| Project docs | Locked SEO H1 + Free Audit path; verified claims only; BrowserMockup as product preview |

Canonical research already in: [Design-Inspiration.md](obsidian/07-UX/Design-Inspiration.md), [Niche-Website-Standards.md](obsidian/09-Research/Niche-Website-Standards.md), [2026-09-02-homepage-redesign-brief.md](.cursor/plans/2026-09-02-homepage-redesign-brief.md), [SITE-SEO-MAP.md](docs/seo/SITE-SEO-MAP.md).

## Chosen visual direction (default)

**Split composition + one dominant macOS BrowserMockup** (Cursor product calm + Olifant split). Desktop: macOS only in hero. Mobile: iOS only (or macOS alone if iOS feels cramped)—never both stacked. Matches [Browser-Mockup-Spec.md](obsidian/07-UX/Browser-Mockup-Spec.md) and fixes current dual-stack clutter.

## Current problems (Observed)

In [hero-section.tsx](src/components/sections/hero-section.tsx) + [homepage.json](content/config/homepage.json):

1. H1 uses `text-h1` (too small for first viewport vs boutique peers)
2. Three text blocks (headline + sub + long differentiation) = wall of copy for 30+ scanners
3. Navy primary CTA blends with brand chrome; header already uses accent Free Audit
4. Dual BrowserMockup stack (macOS + iOS) overcrowds first viewport
5. Trust line uses `|` pipe characters; no partner badge in hero
6. No secondary calm path (phone / text link) for deliberative buyers

## Target hero composition (first viewport)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph left [CopyColumn]
    Eyebrow[Optional eyebrow Verified Partner]
    H1[Outcome H1 display scale]
    Sub[One short supporting sentence]
    CTA[Accent Free Audit plus ArrowRight]
    Trust[Trust line since 2018 plus badge]
  end
  subgraph right [VisualColumn]
    Mock[Single macOS BrowserMockup PPC tab]
  end
  left --> right
```

**Budget (aligned with your landing rules):** brand signal + one headline + one support sentence + one CTA group + one dominant visual. Stats stay in the next sections—not inside hero.

## Copy plan (keep SEO H1; tighten body)

| Element | Decision |
|---------|----------|
| H1 | **Keep locked:** `Full-service Amazon growth for ambitious FBA brands` ([SITE-SEO-MAP.md](docs/seo/SITE-SEO-MAP.md)) |
| Subheadline | Keep one service sentence; cut or demote long `differentiation` paragraph (move idea into sub or a single calm line under CTA—not a third paragraph) |
| Primary CTA | `Get Free Audit` → `/free-audit-2/` with `variant="accent"` + lucide `ArrowRight` |
| Secondary | Text link: phone (`tel:`) or “Talk with our team” → `/contact/` (deliberative 30+ path) |
| Trust | Verified Partner + since 2018; partner badge image if asset exists; **no Unicode pipes**—CSS separator or plain words |
| Eyebrow | Optional small text: `Amazon Ads Verified Partner` (not a floating chip overlay on the mockup) |

## Implementation work

### 1. Content

Update hero `data` in [content/config/homepage.json](content/config/homepage.json):

- Trim differentiation (fold into subheadline or one short line)
- Add optional `secondaryCta` / phone fields if schema allows, or render from site config phone
- Visual variants: desktop macOS only in config; component handles responsive swap to iOS

### 2. UI — [hero-section.tsx](src/components/sections/hero-section.tsx)

- Display-scale H1 (`text-display` or dedicated hero class with fluid clamp ~40–56px)
- Wider left column breathing room; tighten vertical rhythm
- Accent CTA + ArrowRight; secondary text action (underline pattern per design system secondary button)
- Render **one** mockup: `lg+` macos / `<lg` ios using existing `BrowserMockup`
- Optional partner badge beside trust line ([design-system brand / partner assets](content/config/design-system.json))
- Subtle section atmosphere: soft gradient or surface tint on shell—not purple/cream AI defaults; use brand navy/orange tokens only
- Motion: 2–3 restrained cues (mockup fade/lift, CTA lift already in PrimaryButton)—respect `prefers-reduced-motion`

### 3. Schema / types if needed

Extend [homepage.schema.ts](src/domain/content/schemas/homepage.schema.ts) only if secondary CTA is config-driven (prefer config over hardcoding).

| Attribute | Observed |

**Skip:** Copying serif brand system; multi-marketplace claim inflation we cannot match; floating social icons clutter.

| Attribute | Observed |

You have access to tools through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers, using `GetDynamicTools` and `CallDynamicTool`.

## Dynamic Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetDynamicTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallDynamicTool` to invoke one tool. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one discovery call followed by one invocation.

If the user mentions a product or service represented by an available namespace, and the request likely depends on it, proactively inspect that namespace before answering. If you are unsure which namespace matches, search with a relevant pattern.

`GetDynamicTools` supports these modes:

1. `{"namespace":"<id>"}`: returns schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. `{"namespace":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns one tool schema with its full description.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches namespace and tool names.
4. `{"namespace":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tools within one namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

Always inspect a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallDynamicTool`.

If the available dynamic tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. ALWAYS call search_design_system first to find existing components, variables, and styles to reuse — never generate components from scratch if a design system match exists.
3. For web app pages, use both tools in parallel: generate_figma_design to capture a pixel-perfect screenshot, and use_figma to build the screen from imported design system components. Refine use_figma output against the screenshot, then delete the screenshot reference.
4. For non-web targets (iOS, Android, generic UI), use use_figma with search_design_system.
5. For updating or syncing a Figma page that has already been captured, use use_figma — even if the source code has changed.

FROM-SCRATCH DESIGN WORKFLOW (no source design or code):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. Call search_design_system and get_libraries to find existing components, tokens, and styles. Build from these primitives.
3. Use create_new_file if no target file exists, then use_figma to assemble the design from design system components.

DESIGN SYSTEM / LIBRARY WORKFLOW:
- To build or extend a design system in Figma from a codebase, load the /figma-generate-library skill.
- To map Figma components to codebase components, load the /figma-code-connect skill.

READING SKILLS:
To load a Figma skill's guidance, call the get_figma_skill tool with the skill's skill:// URI. get_figma_skill reads one resource per call. Start from the skill index (skill://index.json), then read a skill's guidance (skill://figma/<skill-name>/SKILL.md). A SKILL.md's relative links (e.g. references/foo.md) are themselves resources: read them as skill://figma/<skill-name>/references/<path>.

GENERATIVE PLUGIN AND SHADER CAPABILITIES:
- Create, list, read, and update generative plugins in the authenticated user's account library (create_generative_plugin, list_generative_plugins, get_generative_plugin, update_generative_plugin).
- Create, list, read, and update shader effects and fills in the authenticated user's account library (create_shader, list_shaders, get_shader, update_shader).

Use this server when the user asks to build, create, upload, publish, or update a Figma generative plugin, Figma plugin, custom tool, shader effect, shader fill, custom effect, custom fill, or procedural shader. These tools manage generative plugins and shaders in the account library; they do not install existing Figma Community plugins.

AUTHORING PREREQUISITES:
- Before calling create_shader or update_shader, load /figma-shaders; resource fallback: skill://figma/figma-shaders/SKILL.md.
- Before calling create_generative_plugin or update_generative_plugin, load /figma-generative-plugins; resource fallback: skill://figma/figma-generative-plugins/SKILL.md.
Read resource fallbacks with resources/read, or use get_figma_skill when resources/read is unavailable." source="mcp" />
